newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail edges down after Q4 warning.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail edges down after Q4 warning.

text.p: Shares in Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd lost seven cents to NZ$8.65 on Friday after the company painted a gloomy picture for fourth quarter freight-related earnings.
Rail operator Tranz Rail said on Thursday, as part of its third quarter report, that lower freight volumes were likely to reduce earnings over the current quarter.
Net profits were up NZ$ 6.2 million to NZ$20.6 million in the period reported to March 31.
Its freight warning arose from problems on the West Coast, where key customer Solid Energy is shipping out less coal due to order deferrals and cancellations, analysts said.
"It's more or less come about at the margin from what is happening in the coal game," said one analyst, who declined to be identified.
"But it will pass. It's just a temporary problem that Coal Corp (now Solid Energy) is having, so it's more or less a one-off profit effect," he said.
Nigel Scott at BZW said the depressed freight outlook should have come as no surprise as it had been well telegraphed to the market weeks before the result, including in a Reuters interview.
He doubted there would be further selling in Tranz Rail, or the other stock market leaders, after an overnight improvement in fundamentals through lower interest and exchange rates.
Tranz Rail, which is 22.48 percent owned by U.S.-based rail freight operator Wisconsin Central, traded in the U.S at US$17 1/2 (NZ$8.56), down 1/4, on high volume.
The ADS shares trade in groups of three equivalent ordinary shares.
